narration: Twelve million Americans walk into a payday loan shop every year thinking it's a quick fix. Here's the trap they walk into.
visual: Person silhouette walking toward a neon-lit 'PAYDAY LOANS' storefront at night. '12 MILLION AMERICANS / TRAPPED YEARLY' text above in white and red.

narration: The average loan is $375 for two weeks with a $56 fee. Sounds fine — until you realize that's a 400% annual interest rate.
visual: Receipt-style document slides in showing '$375 borrowed', '2 WEEK TERM', '$56 FEE' (counting up). Large red stamp '400% APR' rotates onto the screen.

narration: Number one: 80% of borrowers can't pay it back on the due date. So they roll it over — and pay that fee all over again.
visual: Calendar showing 14-day due date slides in on left. Circular rollover arrows spin on right with '$56' at center. 'ROLLOVER' text pulses in red.

narration: Number two: the average borrower takes out 8 loans per year, all trying to pay off the first one. That $375 emergency costs $521 in fees.
visual: Eight loan document cards stack one by one. Running fee counter below climbs to $521. Most recent card highlighted in red.

narration: Number three: payday lenders pull in $9 billion profit every year. They don't make money on fast repayers — just the ones stuck in the cycle.
visual: Pink piggy bank with growing crack on left, money stream flows right to a bank building. '$9B / YEAR' counter animates up in red.

narration: Credit unions offer emergency loans at 18% APR — not 400%. Search 'emergency loan credit union' before you ever walk through that door.
visual: Two side-by-side boxes: red 'PAYDAY LOAN 400% APR' with X mark vs green 'CREDIT UNION 18% APR' with checkmark. Black CTA bar at bottom.
